resources.string: Use Add app for apps, or Add custom slot for displays, inputs and commands. Choose a component and behavior to see instructions and examples below. After saving, tap Done to return to the panel.
Choosing a component

Button: run a command on tap
Display: show results, fixed text or an HTML view
Entry: pass text, save notes or use a shell
Choice: select a value from prepared options
Switch: read and change a state
List: act on a command-generated list

Connect entries and choices → a button → a result display to build a form.
Runs a command when tapped. Start with a label and command. Use Connections to choose input values or a result display.
A button that shows ON/OFF. Set the commands to turn it on and off, then choose how to read its state. A state command should print on or off.
Displays a button’s output. Save this field, then select it under Connections → Result display in the button editor. No command is needed here.
Displays a fixed value. Enter the content in Initial or fixed value. A connected button can also pass it as an argument.
Runs a command when opened and displays its text output. For example, date shows the current date and time. Set automatic refresh in Advanced settings.

Displays HTML inside the panel. Set a macro that calls z2-view, or a command that opens a prepared HTML file. Create page.html first for the example below. Choose manual or automatic refresh. Macros define forms and action buttons. Save, then tap Done to see the view.
Passes text entered by the user to another component. Save this field, then select it as an input under Connections in the button editor. Set a default or make input required if needed.
Lets the user choose from prepared values. Separate options with |, save, then select this field under Connections in the button editor. The default must match one of the options.
A note that saves what you write. Leave the file path empty to get started. Content remains after closing the panel and can be passed to a connected button.
Type text and tap Send to pass it to the command as standard input. For example, cat returns the entered text unchanged.

Use a shell inside the panel. No command is needed in this editor. Save and tap Done to start typing. The shell, output and draft remain after closing. Use a regular terminal tab for interactive programs.
Reads and changes the current state. The state command should print on or off; the run command should toggle it. The state is read again after the action.

Turns each output line into a selectable item. Tapping a row runs the selection command, which receives the value as \"$1\". To use different labels and values, print label + tab + value on each line.
Enter a shell command available on this device. Pick an installed macro below and append any arguments it needs. Check it in a regular terminal tab first.

Empty or 0 disables periodic refresh. A value of 5–86400 seconds refreshes only while the panel is visible. Views repeat the display command; macros can define a different action for the manual Refresh button.
Empty means 30 seconds. Increase to 1–300 seconds for slower work such as network requests.
Empty uses a file dedicated to this item. To use an existing file, specify a path inside the app’s shared home.
The value used when opened. For a choice field, use one of its options.
Separate options with |. Empty or duplicate options are not allowed.
Empty uses the component default. Set 1–20 lines to choose the display height.
Empty means automatic. A number uses dp; % uses the column width or panel height.
Example: %1$s
Use example
